page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine based on AMD EPYC 7B13 silicon. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to a single dedicated physical core running 2 threads. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 4.0 GB per core ratio. Cache structure includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector extensions are limited to standard AVX, with no AVX-512 or AMX support present. The configuration does not include local disk storage, dedicated hardware GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 networking.

Performance benchmarks show an instance weighted toward baseline single-threaded tasks. Single-core tests achieve mid-tier marks, with a stress-ng score of 2669.58, Geekbench score of 1463.0, and 25.9 GB/s throughput in gzip compression. In contrast, aggregate parallel compute and memory throughput sit in lower percentiles. The Geekbench multi-core score reaches 1812.0, while large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth measure 26.64 GB/s and 20.4 GB/s respectively. Database operations and Redis caching record entry-level throughput, with Redis executing 2.04 million operations per second.

Because computing capacity is confined to two threads on one core, multi-threaded scaling is naturally restricted. The instance delivers cost efficiency through dedicated baseline execution without burst metering, making it suitable for low-intensity continuous operations. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web frontends, development testing nodes, entry-level continuous integration tasks, and basic background data transformations that do not demand expansive memory or sustained parallel processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, backed by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES, and standard AVX support, while omitting AVX-512 instructions. The instance provides no bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. In benchmark testing, the system delivers balanced single-core compute performance, performing reliably in single-threaded decompression and compression routines. However, the dual-thread design yields lower-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth scores. This instance provides a cost-effective platform for low-concurrency operations, including lightweight web serving, small staging environments, simple background jobs, and continuous integration workers that require predictable, non-burstable CPU allocation.
